intro: What to expect when you work with us. Architectural projects and approvals involve many stages and have complicated procedures. Here is our guide to show you how it is organized, along with benchmarks, timelines, and anticipated costs. We look forward to working with you!

phases.name: Schematic Design & Preliminary Pricing
phases.purpose: Establish building program, space requirements, design direction
phases.timeline: Usually 1–4 months for a single-family home
tasks: Site visit to measure building / documentation of field conditions and input into CAD format
Create schematic level floor plans, hand-sketched perspectives, with discussion on finishes
Explore different design directions and select one
Preliminary pricing from Owner’s general contractor (if desired) and design approval by client before proceeding to next phase

phases.name: Design Development & Construction Documents
phases.purpose: Develop the schematic design and prepare construction documents
phases.timeline: Usually 1–4 months for a single-family home
tasks: Finalize site, floor and reflected ceiling plans (including electrical and lighting), elevations, sections, details, schedules and specifications as required
Prepare Planning Review Application, if required

phases.name: Permitting & Final Pricing
phases.purpose: Obtain city or county approval for construction
phases.timeline: Bid documents 2–4 weeks · Permit processing 2–12 months · Pricing 3–4 weeks · Bidding 4–6 weeks
tasks: Submit building permit application or addendum and respond to agency comments and code interpretations
Assist with final pricing and/or prepare bid documents
Answer contractor questions and help select and prepare construction contract documents
required: Consultant documents (structural, lighting, mechanical and electrical as required)

phases.name: Construction Administration
phases.purpose: Administer the construction contract and represent the client
phases.meetings: Bi-weekly site visits with the contractor
tasks: Site visits as required to observe construction

phases.name: Completion
phases.purpose: Close out the project, with photography and possible publication
